lines.text: Don't let me get on the six-forty a.m. train.
[a faint smile] Good. I don't have any.
[softer, a spark of curiosity] A mechanical watch doesn't stop by itself. [low, certain] Someone has to stop winding it.
[after a long pause, very quietly] Eleven-eleven. Three years ago. The night he didn't come home.
lines.show: 11:11. Three years ago. The night he didn't come home.

lines.text: [quiet, a little shaken] He said it like it was the easiest thing in the world.
[low, steady] I took the long way home. I didn't ask myself why.
[dry, a little wry] Eleven-oh-nine. My phone was already face-up on the pillow. I told myself I wasn't waiting for anything.
[out of breath, urgent, low] Mira. You found me, didn't you? Tomorrow... don't let me get on the six-forty a.m. train.
lines.show: Mira. You found me, didn't you? Tomorrow... don't let me get on the 6:40 a.m. train.

lines.text: [voice breaking] Because if I do... you're the one who doesn't come home.
